accordions.heading: What is syphilis?
accordions.content:
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection. It can cause symptoms such as a painless sore or rash, but some people have no noticeable symptoms at all. Symptoms can also disappear even though the infection is still present.

Syphilis can be treated and cured with antibiotics.

accordions.heading: Is this for you?
accordions.content:
You don’t need to have symptoms to test. Syphilis can cause no noticeable symptoms.

It may be worth testing if:
checklist: You have a new sexual partner, or more than one
A sexual partner has told you they have syphilis or another STI
You have possible symptoms, such as a painless sore or rash

benefits.text: Everything you need to test for syphilis at home:

how.heading: How does the test work?
how.intro:
The test looks for antibodies your body can produce in response to syphilis infection, using a small finger-prick blood sample.

Your result appears on the test cassette in around 15 minutes, with no sample to send to a laboratory.

steps.title: Prick your finger
steps.text: Wash your hands and clean your fingertip with an alcohol pad. Let it dry, then use the lancet to prick your finger and form a drop of blood.

steps.title: Add blood and diluent
steps.text: Use the pipette to collect your blood. Add 3 drops of blood to the sample well marked “S” on the test pad. Then add 1 drop of sample diluent to the same well.

steps.title: Read your result
steps.text: Read your result between 10 and 20 minutes. Don't read the test after 20 minutes, as the result may no longer be reliable.

windows.heading: When should I test?
windows.subheading: You can test now. If your result is negative within 12 weeks of exposure, repeat at 12 weeks.
windows.initialTitle: Test now. If negative, repeat in 12 weeks.

questions.question: How soon after sex can I test for syphilis?
questions.answer:
You can take the test at any time, but testing too early can give a negative result even if you have syphilis. If it has been less than 12 weeks since the sexual contact you're concerned about and your result is negative, test again once 12 weeks have passed.

If you have symptoms or know you've been exposed to syphilis, contact a sexual health clinic without waiting 12 weeks.

questions.question: How reliable is this syphilis rapid test?
questions.answer:
When used correctly, this test provides a reliable way to check for syphilis antibodies at home. 99.81% of results matched laboratory testing in a clinical evaluation.

Testing too soon after exposure can affect your result, so an early negative may need to be repeated. This is a screening test, so a positive result should be followed up with a sexual health clinic for further testing.

questions.question: What does a negative syphilis test result mean?
questions.answer: A negative result means syphilis antibodies were not detected by the test. If your possible exposure was within the last 12 weeks, you may have tested too early. Test again at 12 weeks. If you have symptoms or are still concerned, speak to a sexual health clinic.

questions.question: What if my result is positive?
questions.answer:
A positive result means syphilis antibodies were detected, but it doesn't necessarily mean you have an active infection.

Contact a sexual health clinic as soon as possible for further testing. They'll explain your result and whether you need treatment.

Syphilis can be cured with antibiotics. If you've had syphilis before, let the clinic know, as antibodies can remain even after successful treatment.

NHS sexual health services are free and confidential.

questions.question: Can I use this syphilis test if I’ve had syphilis before?
questions.answer: If you’ve had syphilis before, this test may still show a positive result even after successful treatment. This is because syphilis antibodies can remain in your blood after the infection has been treated. Speak to a sexual health clinic about the right test for you.

questions.question: Can I take a syphilis test while pregnant?
questions.answer: If you’re pregnant and concerned about syphilis, speak to your midwife, GP or a sexual health clinic. Syphilis testing is routinely offered during pregnancy through the NHS.
